title: One number, many forms
description:
Print a number in decimal, hex and binary, and the bytes it is stored as.

```
Number: 1000
decimal 1000
hex     0x3E8
binary  0000 0011 1110 1000
bytes in memory: E8 03 00 00 (little-endian)
```
hints: `reinterpret_cast` tells the compiler to treat an address as pointing at a different type, without changing the bits. `const auto* bytes{reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(&n)};` lets you read `n` one byte at a time, `bytes[0]` to `bytes[3]`; reading any object through `unsigned char` is always allowed.
`std::bitset<16>{static_cast<unsigned>(n)}.to_string()` gives the bits; insert a space every 4 characters.
requirements: Read an `int`; print hex with `std::hex` and binary with `std::bitset<16>` grouped in fours.
Print the 4 bytes in memory order by reading the variable through an `unsigned char*`.
stretch: Show a negative number and explain the bytes you see.
